unsupported_claims: LINE(1st+2nd) is only applied to supervised tasks is the core point; the AI answer instead says LINE does not require supervised data, contradicting the evidence that LINE(1st+2nd) is only applied to supervised tasks because weights are hard to set unsupervised.
The claim that LINE is evaluated with labels only downstream and that labels are used only for evaluation omits that the paper restricts the concatenated LINE(1st+2nd) variant to supervised tasks.
The claim that LINE's original paper used Flickr, YouTube, Orkut, and Twitter is not contained in the evidence and is offered from memory.
The claim that DeepWalk's original paper reports BlogCatalog results is not stated in the provided evidence, though the evidence shows this paper's BlogCatalog evaluation.
The claim that DeepWalk is evaluated with a one-vs-rest logistic regression on 10%-90% training ratios with Micro/Macro-F1 averaged over random splits is supported by the evidence.
rationale: The answer correctly describes the DeepWalk BlogCatalog evaluation protocol (training ratio 10%-90%, Macro/Micro-F1, one-vs-rest logistic regression), but it misses the key point from the evidence that LINE(1st+2nd) is applied only to supervised tasks because dimension weights are hard to set unsupervised. It also adds uncited claims about LINE's datasets and DeepWalk's original reporting.
